title: Single-molecule Fluorescence in situ Hybridization (smFISH) for RNA Detection in Adherent Animal Cells.
markdown:
## Protocol: Single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization for quantifying RNA transcripts in adherent mammalian cells

### Overview

This protocol outlines the procedure for single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) to quantify RNA transcripts in adherent mammalian cells. It covers reagent preparation, probe design and labeling, cell culture setup, the FISH workflow including fixation, permeabilization, hybridization, washing, and mounting, as well as imaging parameters and data analysis using FISH-quant software.

### Materials/Reagents

PBSM buffer, Fixation buffer (PFA), Quenching buffer (glycine), Permeabilization buffer (Surfact-Amps X-100), Pre-hybridization buffer (Formamide, SSC), Hybridization buffer (Formamide, E. coli tRNA, Dextran Sulfate, BSA, SSC, VRC), DAPI stain solution, Culture media, 1x PBS, 70% ethanol, Fibronectin (optional coating), Pro-Long anti-fade solution, Stellaris RNA FISH probes or DNA oligos with amine ends/amine reactive dye/enzymatic labeling reagents.

### Equipment

Bio-safety cabinet, Cell culture incubator, Chemical (fume) hood, 12-well plates, Coverslips, Tweezers, Kimwipes, Plastic box/dish for hybridization chamber, Parafilm, Aluminum foil, Wide-field microscope, MATLAB software, FISH-quant software.

### Safety & Sterility

Work in a bio-safety cabinet for sterile cell culture. Wear gloves, use barrier tips, and avoid RNase contamination surfaces during FISH steps. Perform all work with PFA and formamide solutions in a chemical (fume) hood due to safety hazards. Protect DAPI and probes from light. Seal hybridization chambers to maintain humidity and protect from light.

## Reagent Preparation

### Pre-Experiment: Reagent and Buffer Preparation

1. Prepare 500 ml of PBSM buffer by mixing 50 ml of 10x PBS, 2.5 ml of 1 M MgCl2, and 475 ml of nuclease-free water. Store at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare 8 ml of fresh fixation buffer by mixing 7 ml of PBSM and 1 ml of 32% PFA. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare 10 ml of fresh quenching buffer by mixing 9.5 ml of PBSM and 0.5 ml of 2 M glycine. Prepare fresh immediately before use as it is prone to microbial contamination. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare stock solutions in advance: a) PBSM buffer according to Recipe 1, and b) a 2 M glycine stock solution in water, filter sterilized, and stored at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Prepare 100 ml of permeabilization buffer by mixing 10 ml of 10x PBS, 1 ml of 10% Surfact-Amps X-100, and 89 ml of nuclease-free water. Store at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Prepare 10 ml of pre-hybridization (Pre-hyb) buffer by mixing 1 ml of 20x SSC, 1 ml of formamide (warmed to room temperature before use), and 8 ml of nuclease-free water. Prepare fresh. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Prepare 1 ml of hybridization buffer by mixing the following components: 0.1 ml of formamide (final 10%), 0.1 ml of competitor (10 mg/ml E. coli tRNA, final 1 mg/ml), 0.5 ml of 20% Dextran Sulfate (final 10%), 10 µl of 20 mg/ml BSA (final 0.2 mg/ml), 0.1 ml of 20x SSC (final 2x), 10 µl of 200 mM VRC (final 2 mM), and 0.18 ml of nuclease-free water. Store at -20 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
8. Prepare stock solutions in advance: 1) A 10 mg/ml E. coli tRNA solution in nuclease-free water, stored at -20 °C; and 2) A 20% Dextran sulfate solution in water (allow 30-60 minutes for complete dissolution due to viscosity), stored at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
9. Assemble the hybridization chamber: a) Use a plastic box or dish large enough to accommodate all coverslips with at least a few millimeters between them; b) Place parafilm on the bottom, avoiding wrinkles under coverslip positions; c) Optionally draw a grid where each square fits one coverslip and label squares; d) Place a cap from a 15 ml conical tube at the edge of the chamber and fill it with 1 ml of water or buffer to maintain humidity; e) Prepare a piece of parafilm to seal the chamber after placing coverslips; f) Prepare aluminum foil to cover the chamber to protect from light. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->
10. Prepare 200 ml of DAPI stain solution by mixing 20 ml of 20x SSC, 10 µl of 10 mg/ml DAPI stock (resulting in a final concentration of 0.5 µg/ml), and 180 ml of nuclease-free water. Store at 4 °C in the dark. Prepare the 10 mg/ml DAPI stock solution in water in advance and store at -20 °C in the dark. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S10 -->

## Probe Design and Labeling

### Probe Design and Labeling

1. Obtain the sense strand RNA sequence of interest to begin probe design. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Use the Stellaris probe design web tool to insert the sense strand sequence and select parameters including organism, specificity level, number of probes, probe length, and minimal spacing. We recommend selecting the highest specificity level (5), 48 probes of 20 nucleotides, and 2 nucleotide spacing as defaults. If fewer than 25 probes are generated, adjust parameters until satisfied. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Label the probes using one of the following methods: order pre-labeled Stellaris RNA FISH probes from Biosearch Technologies (recommended for consistency and ease, though expensive); order DNA oligos with amine ends and label with an amine-reactive dye (works for 20 nt oligos, relatively expensive); or enzymatically label the probes (cheaper option). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. Suspend the oligo probe set in nuclease-free water (prepare a 25 µM solution for Stellaris probes) and keep at -20 °C in the dark. Aliquot into 10-20 µl volumes to minimize freeze-thaw cycles, although multiple freeze-thaw cycles have not been observed to cause noticeable deterioration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->

## Cell Culture

### Cell Culture Setup

> **Operational constraint:** Perform all sterile cell culture work inside a bio-safety cabinet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
1. Pre-warm 1x PBS and culture media to 37 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
2. If coating coverslips is required, prepare a coating solution, such as diluting fibronectin 1:100 in 1x PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
3. Place one coverslip in each well of a 12-well plate for each sample. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
4. Wash each coverslip briefly with 1 ml of 70% ethanol and aspirate. Then wash briefly with 1 ml of sterile 1x PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
5. If coating, add 1 ml of coating solution to each well and incubate as required (e.g., 10-20 minutes in a cell culture incubator for fibronectin). Remove the coating solution and wash once with 1 ml of PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->
6. Add 1 ml of culture media per well and seed the chosen adherent cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S07 -->
7. Culture the cells in a cell culture incubator for the required duration. Do not allow cultures to become confluent; aim for approximately 80%-90% confluence at the time of fixation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S08 -->

## FISH Protocol

### FISH: General Safety and Handling

> **Operational constraint:** To prevent RNase contamination, wear gloves, use barrier tips, and avoid working on surfaces regularly used for RNase-containing procedures (e.g., plasmid prep kits). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Perform all handling of PFA and formamide solutions in a chemical (fume) hood for safety. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Pipet liquids onto the wall of the well rather than directly onto the cells. For cells with delicate structures (e.g., dendrites, membrane nanotubes), use a pipet aid at the slowest setting and do not use a vacuum aspirator. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Do not shake the 12-well plate during wash steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->

### FISH: Fixation and Permeabilization

1. Wash cells with PBSM using three quick rinses. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S01 -->
2. Fix cells by incubating with freshly prepared fixation buffer for 10 minutes at room temperature. Do not exceed this duration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S02 -->
3. Wash cells with quenching buffer for 10 minutes at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S03 -->
4. Wash cells with PBSM for 10 minutes at room temperature and repeat this step. Cells may be stored overnight at 4 °C at this stage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S04 -->
5. Permeabilize cells by incubating with permeabilization buffer for 10 minutes at room temperature. Do not exceed this duration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S05 -->
6. Wash cells with PBSM for 10 minutes at room temperature and repeat this step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S06 -->

### FISH: Hybridization

1. Incubate cells with pre-hybridization buffer for 30 minutes at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T2-S01 -->
2. While waiting (Step C7), mix the pre-made hybridization buffer with the probes, and prepare the

 hybridization chamber (see Recipes and Note 2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T2-S02 -->
3. Place 45 µl of the hybridization buffer mixture at each intended coverslip position within the hybridization chamber. Avoid small foam-like bubbles, but large bubbles do not need to be removed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T2-S03 -->
4. Using tweezers, gently lift each coverslip from the well, remove excess liquid by touching the edge on a Kimwipe, and place the coverslips with the cell-side facing down onto the hybridization buffer drops. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T2-S04 -->
5. Seal the hybridization chamber with Parafilm, wrap with aluminum foil, and place in a 37 °C incubator for 3 hours to overnight. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T2-S05 -->

### FISH: Post-Hybridization Washes

1. Prepare a new (or reuse the same) 12-well plate containing pre-hybridization buffer. Using tweezers, transfer the coverslips back into the plate with the cell-side facing up. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S01 -->
2. Cover the plate with aluminum foil and incubate in the 37 °C incubator for 15 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S02 -->
3. Wash the coverslips again in pre-hybridization buffer for 15 minutes at 37 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S03 -->
4. Rinse quickly with 2x SSC at room temperature (three quick rinses). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S04 -->
5. Stain the cells in DAPI stain solution (pre-warmed to room temperature) for 1 minute at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S05 -->
6. Wash the coverslips for 5 minutes with 2x SSC. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S06 -->

### FISH: Slide Mounting and Storage

1. During this final wash step, prepare microscope slides in the cardboard tray:

 a. Label the slide(s).

 b. Just before lifting the coverslips, add 20 µl of Pro-Long anti-fade solution for each cover slip

 (there can be two per slide). Remove any air bubbles. See also Note 4. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T4-S01 -->
2. Use tweezers to lift the coverslips, remove excess liquid, and place them cell-side facing down onto the Pro-Long anti-fade drop on the slide. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T4-S02 -->
3. Allow the slides to dry at room temperature in the dark for at least several hours. For optimal image quality, wait more than 24 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T4-S03 -->
4. For long-term storage, optionally seal the edges of the coverslip with nail polish after the Pro-Long has dried. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T4-S04 -->
5. Store slides at room temperature for several days (up to at least one week) or at -20 °C for long-term storage (months to years). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T4-S05 -->

## Imaging

### Imaging

> **Operational constraint:** Ensure all slides from the same experiment are imaged using identical microscope conditions. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
1. Perform imaging on any wide-field microscope as specified in the equipment section. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->
2. Capture images in descending color order by wavelength (e.g., Cy5 at 670 nm, Cy3 at 570 nm, Alexa488 at 520 nm, and DAPI at 460 nm). This order is critical because imaging through the DAPI channel can induce granular autofluorescence in other channels in certain cell types (e.g., MEFs, HEK293T), which has been reproduced across multiple microscopes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S03 -->
3. Set exposure parameters: For FISH channels, use maximum (100%) light source power and an exposure time of 1-3 seconds. For DAPI, use low power (e.g., 30%) and a very short exposure time (e.g., 20-40 ms). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S04 -->
4. Adjust exposure time and parameters to balance photon collection for spot detection against increased background fluorescence. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S05 -->
5. Collect multiple Z-sections to detect RNA spots throughout the cell volume. Use Z-steps of 0.2-0.3 µm and collect at least 30 sections for flat cells (e.g., fibroblasts) or more (e.g., 41 sections for HEK293T or N87 cells). Image all Z-sections for one channel completely before switching to the next channel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S06 -->
6. Set pixel binning to 1 x 1 for better resolution, or use 2 x 2 binning if signal enhancement is prioritized over resolution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S07 -->

## Data Analysis

### FISH-quant Software Setup

1. Install MATLAB and then install the FISH-quant software. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. In FISH-quant, select the main folder, images folder, outlines folder, and results folder. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->
3. Insert experimental parameters: XY pixel size (based on camera and binning), Z pixel size, refractive index of the immersion oil, numerical aperture (NA) of the objective, and excitation/emission wavelengths of the FISH probe fluorophore. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S03 -->
4. Under Tools -> outline designer, draw outlines for cells, nuclei, and transcription sites (TS). Use automatic detection features based on DAPI staining for nuclei and TS/FISH staining for transcription sites. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S04 -->
5. Upload the created outline file to the image. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S05 -->
6. Filter the background by testing different modes and parameters to achieve the best filtering result. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S06 -->
7. Perform pre-detection according to the software instructions. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S07 -->
8. Fit spots using the Gaussian algorithm. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S08 -->
9. Adjust thresholding parameters to achieve the best detection results. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S09 -->
10. Save the detection settings. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S10 -->

### Batch Processing and Inspection

1. Use Tools -> Batch processing to analyze multiple images. Modify thresholding parameters after batch analysis to fine-tune results. Set parameters so that negative controls yield close to zero detected spots. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S01 -->
2. Use Tools -> Spot inspector to manually eliminate obvious false positives, such as areas of high autofluorescence. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S02 -->
3. Save the FISH-quant data as a '.txt' file. Copy and paste the data into Excel for further analysis. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S03 -->
